body:
I think this is probably Taffy related. It seems to round the length of certain nodes but not others.

There are subtle problems with Bevy UI Text that are similar where what I suspect is happening is that you ask for a width of x pixels for your text with the MeasureFunc, but then Taffy rounds it down a pixel and so the Text no longer fits the width, so the last word of the text gets pushed down to a new line. But the Node itself stays at a height of only one line of text, so the text renderer doesn't draw the second line of text and it just looks there are missing words at the end of sentences with certain text layouts.

Hmm... I feel like the text renderer probably shouldn't count a glyph as fitting if it requires a partial pixel.

>  I think this is probably Taffy related. It seems to round the length of certain nodes but not others.

Taffy's rouding is pretty simple. It computes the entire layout using floats, and then rounds everything at the end.

I haven't really looked at this deeply yet, so I might be completely off. The scale factor code is all over the place, it might be something there. I'll recreate some of my examples just in Taffy and compare what happens.

I can see why this is happening. Unrounded results for @A-Walrus's test:

```
TREE
└──  FLEX [x: 0    y: 0    width: 963.3333 height: 1000] (3v1)
    ├──  LEAF [x: 381.36664 y: 0    width: 100.3 height: 100.3] (1v1)
    └──  LEAF [x: 481.66663 y: 0    width: 100.3 height: 100.3] (2v1)
```

child_a's x position is going to get rounded down. child_b's x position is going to get rounded up. It's not immediately obvious to me what the correct solution is though. Especially as I suspect the ideal solution would take into account the `devicePixelRatio` and round based on the size of physical pixels rather than logical ones, and perhaps even do subpixel rendering.

This quote quite neatly sums up the problem:

>  We’re trying to meet a bunch of constraints that can’t all be satisfied at the same time (the proof is left as an exercise to the reader, though I may have actually written it out once in a Bugzilla comment):
> 1. 4 adjacent objects of width/height 25% (for example) starting at one edge of a container should end exactly at the other edge; there should never be an extra pixel in the container and they should never be wrapped due to being a pixel to wide
> 2. objects that are logically adjacent should always touch visually; there should never be a pixel gap or a pixel of overlap due to rounding error
> 3. objects given the same width should occupy the same number of pixels
> 4. object boundaries should always (visually) be aliased to a specific pixel boundary in the display (they should never be blurred)
> 
> The one [Mozilla] sacrifices is typically (3), except for borders where we sacrifice (1) by rounding the widths to pixel boundaries much earlier.

(https://johnresig.com/blog/sub-pixel-problems-in-css/)

I tried looking into what browsers do, but there seems to be no easy way to tell because they won't give you programatic access to the values used for rendering (`getBoundingClientRect` will give you the unrounded floats, and `offsetLeft`/`offsetWidth` will give you values Taffy is already computing with the 1 pixel gap even though there isn't actually a 1px gap in the final render).

Yes, I understand now I think. The size of the root node doesn't matter. If you add another node to the example that wraps the two nodes it will be rounded up to 201 pixels wide, with the extra pixel either between or to the side of the two nodes, depending on the alignment.

# Objective

Fixes #369

## Context

- https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/issues/369
- https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/7712
- https://github.com/facebook/yoga/commit/aa5b296ac78f7a22e1aeaf4891243c6bb76488e2
- https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/pull/145

## Changes Made

- Add `enabled_rounding` and `disable_rounding` method to `Taffy` struct to allow consumers of Taffy to obtain unrounded values if they want them.
- Revert rounding changes from https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/pull/145
- Add test for "no 1px gaps" from #369
- Update gentest runner to use new rounding mode. We're basically just running the same rounding algorithm in JavaScript using float values obtained from Chrome using `getBoundingClientRect`. This is also what Yoga does.
- Special case two tests to run in unrounded mode because they're failing with the new rounding. I have manually verified that this is just due to Taffy's lower precision (only using f32) making it round the other way as that test happens to have values *very* close to exactly `0.5` of a pixel (which isn't too important I don't think).
- Enable two previous disabled tests that came from Yoga (names starting with `rounding_controversy`).

## Feedback wanted

- High-level sense check: does this seems like the correct fix?
- On testing: As we're effectively running the rounding algorithm ourselves in the test generator, it's questionable how value we're actually getting from testing the rounding. The alternative would be to run tests on the float values. We won't get exact equality here, but we could run with something like "difference is < 0.1" which is what I've done for the two failing tests mentioned above. That would allow us to test a little more precisely than we currently are. On the other hand, we have tests that are specifically there to test rounding, for which it would seem silly to omit rouding. Perhaps we should just leave as-is for now and consider converting tests to use floats in future?

issue.body: # Objective fixes #8911, #7712 ## Solution Rounding was added to Taffy which fixed issue #7712. The implementation uses the f32 `round` method which rounds ties (fractional part is a half) away from zero. Issue #8911 occurs when a node's min and max bounds on either axis are "ties" and zero is between them. Then the bounds are rounded away from each other, and the node grows by a pixel. This alone shouldn't cause the node to expand continuously, but I think there is some interaction with the way Taffy recomputes a layout from its cached data that I didn't identify. This PR fixes #8911 by first disabling Taffy's internal rounding and using an alternative rounding function that rounds ties up. Then, instead of rounding the values of the internal layout tree as Taffy's built-in rounding does, we leave those values unmodified and only the values stored in the components are rounded. This requires walking the tree for the UI node geometry update rather than iterating through a query. Because the component values are regenerated each update, that should mean that UI updates are idempotent (ish) now and make the growing node behaviour seen in issue #8911 impossible. I expected a performance regression, but it's an improvement on main: ``` cargo run --profile stress-test --features trace_tracy --example many_buttons ``` I guess it makes sense to do the rounding together with the node size and position updates. --- ## Changelog `bevy_ui::layout`: * Taffy's built-in rounding is disabled and rounding is now performed by `ui_layout_system`. * Instead of rounding the values of the internal layout tree as Taffy's built-in rounding does, we leave those values unmodified and only the values stored in the components are rounded. This requires walking the tree for the UI node geometry update rather than iterating through a query. Because the component values are regenerated each update, that should mean that UI updates are idempotent now and make the growing node behaviour seen in issue #8911 impossible. * Added two helper functions `round_ties_up` and `round_layout_coordinates`.
